newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares set record waiting for West demand.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares set record waiting for West demand.

text.p: Leading Russian shares set a new record on Friday on domestic buying with the market expecting stronger foreign demand on Monday, traders said.
However, operators were worried the market was overheated to the level where foreigners would find it profitbale to sell.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares rose to a new record of 495.57 on $93.49 million in total market volume.

"Our client base is quiet today, New York is silent," a Western trader said. "Today's buying is no doubt Russian operators' buying. Many people are now torturing themselves to figure out how New York will react on Monday."
Regent European Securities trader Alexander Fonarkov said oil company LUKoil's new rating pushed prices higher.
Standard & Poor's assigned LUKoil BB minus foreign currency issuer credit rating and its shares LKOH.RTS rose to $23.65 from $22.50 at Thursady's close.
"Overall there is enthusiuasm about the equity market," he said, though he said growth would likely slow.
"The market is obviously overheated, but our foreign investors and local operators are in a state of euphoria," OPM-Bank analysis department head Mikhail Reznikov said.
UES EESR.RTS power utility rose to $0.4495 from $0.4470, Mosenergo MSNG.RTS power utlity was $1.586 after $1.1545, Rostelekom RTKM.RTS telecoms company rose to $5.06 from $4.69.
